General Surgery Billing

General Surgery Billing Services That Capture Every Dollar Your OR Earns

General surgery billing is built on a 90-day global surgical period framework, and every post-operative visit, related procedure, and ancillary service performed within that window must be correctly classified as bundled or separately billable. Laparoscopic versus open approach codes change reimbursement in every case. Multiple procedures in the same session trigger payment reduction rules. Assistant surgeon claims require specific modifier documentation. ProtoMed's certified general surgery billing specialists handle every case with the precision your practice demands. Fewer denials. Faster reimbursements. More revenue.

Why Choose Us

Stop Losing Surgical Revenue to Global Period Errors and Approach Code Mismatches

General surgery billing involves a structural complexity that creates consistent revenue loss in practices without surgical billing expertise. Every major surgical procedure carries a 90-day global period during which all routine post-operative care is bundled into the surgical fee, but visits for complications, unrelated conditions, and separately identifiable services within that period require specific modifiers to be billed and paid separately. A wound check billed without modifier -24 is denied. An E/M visit for a new medical problem during the global period is separately billable with the right documentation, and lost without it. For practices performing laparoscopic and open procedures, selecting the wrong approach code on a conversion case changes the entire reimbursement amount.

ProtoMed's certified general surgery billing team understands the full complexity of surgical billing: 90-day global period management, laparoscopic versus open approach code selection, multiple procedure payment reduction calculations, assistant and co-surgeon billing with correct modifier application, and the pre-authorization workflows required for elective and urgent surgical cases. We submit clean claims, manage global period tracking across your entire patient panel, and follow up on every denial so your practice collects what it has earned.

Our Expertise

General Surgery Coding Expertise That Reduces Denials

General surgery billing spans laparoscopic and open procedures, abdominal and gastrointestinal surgery, hernia repair, breast surgery, endocrine surgery, and trauma cases, each with distinct approach codes, global period rules, and payer-specific documentation standards. Our certified coders know every code and billing rule across the full general surgery spectrum.

  • CPT 47562–47570

    Laparoscopic cholecystectomy: with and without cholangiography and intraoperative imaging

  • CPT 43239–43289

    Laparoscopic and open foregut surgery: fundoplication, gastrectomy, and bariatric procedures

  • CPT 49505–49659

    Hernia repair: inguinal, umbilical, ventral, incisional, and laparoscopic approaches

  • CPT 19100–19499

    Breast surgery: biopsy, lumpectomy, mastectomy, and sentinel node procedures

  • CPT 60000–60699

    Thyroid and parathyroid surgery: thyroidectomy, parathyroidectomy, and neck dissection

  • Modifier -22 / -80 / -51

    Increased complexity (-22), assistant surgeon (-80), multiple procedures (-51) with discounting

  • Modifier -24 / -25 / -79

    Post-op E/M unrelated (-24), same-day separate E/M (-25), unrelated procedure in global (-79)

Procedure-Specific Billing

Specialized Billing for Every General Surgery Procedure

Each general surgery procedure type carries its own global period rules, approach code selection requirements, and payer documentation standards. ProtoMed's certified team handles every case correctly, from laparoscopic cholecystectomies and hernia repairs to complex abdominal and endocrine cases.

  • 01

    Global Period Management

    The 90-day global surgical period bundles all routine post-operative care into the surgical fee, and every visit within the global period must be correctly classified. Routine wound checks and staple removals are bundled. E/M visits for complications, unrelated medical conditions, or new problems require specific modifiers (-24 for unrelated E/M, -79 for unrelated procedures) to be billed separately. We track 90-day global periods for every surgical case and apply the correct modifiers to protect all separately billable post-operative services.

  • 02

    Laparoscopic vs. Open Approach Billing

    Laparoscopic and open versions of the same procedure carry different CPT codes and different reimbursement rates. When a laparoscopic case is converted to open mid-procedure, the correct billing depends on how much of the laparoscopic approach was completed before conversion. Billing the wrong approach code is a coding error on every case it occurs. We select the correct approach-specific CPT code for every surgical case and handle laparoscopic-to-open conversion billing with the operative note documentation required for clean claim submission.

  • 03

    Multiple Procedure & Complex Case Billing

    When multiple surgical procedures are performed in the same operative session, Medicare and most commercial payers apply a Multiple Procedure Payment Reduction, reimbursing the primary procedure at 100% and secondary procedures at 50%. Modifier -51 signals multiple procedures. Complex cases that significantly exceed the typical work for a procedure qualify for modifier -22 (unusual procedural services) with documentation of the additional time and complexity involved. We calculate MPPR-adjusted expected reimbursements on every multi-procedure case and identify and contest underpayments.

  • 04

    Assistant Surgeon & Co-Surgeon Billing

    When a second surgeon assists during a complex case, the assistant surgeon bills the same CPT code with modifier -80 (or -82 when a qualified resident is unavailable). Co-surgeons who each perform distinct portions of a procedure bill with modifier -62. Payer policies on assistant surgeon billing vary, some require pre-authorization, and some procedures have specific "assistant surgeon not permitted" restrictions. We correctly apply assistant and co-surgeon modifiers, manage payer-specific authorization requirements, and ensure both physician claims are submitted with the documentation needed for payment.

  • 05

    Hernia Repair Billing

    Hernia billing requires precise code selection based on defect type (inguinal, umbilical, ventral, incisional, parastomal), approach (open or laparoscopic), patient age, and whether the hernia is initial or recurrent. Bilateral inguinal hernia repair requires the -50 modifier and the correct bilateral code. Mesh placement may be separately billable depending on the payer and procedure. We accurately select the correct hernia code for every case and capture all separately billable components at their full reimbursement value.

  • 06

    Prior Authorization & Pre-Surgical Billing

    Most elective general surgery procedures require prior authorization, and a missing or expired authorization means a high-value surgical claim is denied regardless of medical necessity. We manage prior authorization requests for all major elective procedures, build clinical documentation packages that satisfy payer criteria, verify coverage and benefits before each case, and confirm authorization status before the patient enters the OR. Proactive authorization management eliminates the most preventable and costly source of surgical claim denials.

Our Process

How ProtoMed's General Surgery Billing Process Works

A structured four-step process that protects surgical revenue across the full case lifecycle, from pre-surgical authorization and eligibility verification through 90-day global period management and final payment posting.

01020304Step 1 of 4
01 · Step 1 of 4

Practice Audit & Revenue Gap Analysis

We review your current general surgery billing setup, identify revenue leaks from global period mismanagement, approach code errors, missing assistant surgeon billing, and unresolved denials, then securely access your existing EHR and OR scheduling system with zero disruption to your surgical operations.

02 · Step 2 of 4

Pre-Surgical Authorization & Eligibility Verification

Before each elective surgical case, we verify patient coverage and benefits, confirm payer-specific surgical authorization requirements, submit prior authorization requests with clinical documentation, and confirm approval before the patient is scheduled. Catching authorization gaps before surgery day eliminates the most costly and preventable source of surgical claim denials.

03 · Step 3 of 4

Case Billing, Global Period Tracking & Claim Submission

Our certified surgical coders review every operative report, select the correct approach-specific CPT codes, calculate MPPR reductions for multi-procedure cases, apply assistant surgeon and co-surgeon modifiers, and establish 90-day global period tracking for every case. Claims are submitted electronically on time to all major payers with the operative documentation needed for first-pass acceptance.

04 · Step 4 of 4

Global Period Management, Denial Appeals & Reporting

Post-operative visits are correctly classified as bundled or separately billable within each patient's active global period. Every denied claim is investigated and appealed with the documentation required for reversal. Payments are posted accurately and you receive clear monthly reports on revenue per case, global period activity, denial patterns, and overall surgical revenue performance.
